I try to push them away, refocus on the weather models, but they linger, like static between signals. I’ve started checking the morning forecast three or four times before the briefing, not because I think it’s wrong, but because I need to be certain. My wife noticed—I used to be able to let things go. Now, I feel like I’m always bracing for something, like there’s a storm building I can’t predict.

And these thoughts—about the people we couldn’t warn in time, about my wife being trapped—just invade my mind, even when I’m trying to focus. But I don’t do anything to “fix” them, no rituals or routines—I just can’t stop seeing it all play out. I can’t sleep, I’m irritable, and I jump at every loud noise.
